chunks: And in the narration of ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAmr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:
I said to him: What do you say regarding the slaughtered animals of the Christians? So he said: There is no harm in them.
I said: But they mention the Messiah over them. He said: They only intended by the Messiah Allah, the Exalted.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating the slaughtered animals of Christians in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on the slaughtered animals of Christians and reports that there is no harm in them. It also explains that when they mention the Messiah, their intended reference is Allah, the Exalted, framing the issue in both legal and theological terms.
